verses.text: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"Tell the people of Israel: Of all the animals that live on land, these are the ones you may eat.
You may eat any animal that has a hoof split in two and also chews the cud.
But some animals only chew the cud or only have split hoofs, and you must not eat them. The camel chews the cud but does not have a split hoof, so it is unclean for you.
The rock badger chews the cud but does not have a split hoof, so it is unclean for you.
The rabbit chews the cud but does not have a split hoof, so it is unclean for you.
The pig has a split hoof, divided in two, but does not chew the cud, so it is unclean for you.
Do not eat their meat or touch their dead bodies. They are unclean for you.
Of all the creatures that live in water, in the seas and the rivers, you may eat any that have fins and scales.
But anything in the seas or rivers that does not have fins and scales, whether small water creatures or any other living thing in the water, is disgusting to you.
You must think of them as disgusting. Do not eat their meat, and think of their dead bodies as disgusting.
Anything in the water that does not have fins and scales is disgusting to you.
These are the birds you must think of as disgusting. Do not eat them, because they are disgusting: the eagle, the vulture, the black vulture,
the red kite, and any kind of black kite,
any kind of raven,
the horned owl, the screech owl, the seagull, and any kind of hawk,
the little owl, the cormorant, the great owl,
the white owl, the desert owl, the osprey,
the stork, any kind of heron, the hoopoe, and the bat.
All flying insects that walk on four legs are disgusting to you.
But you may eat some winged insects that walk on four legs: those with jointed legs above their feet for jumping on the ground.
Of these you may eat any kind of locust, any kind of katydid, any kind of cricket, and any kind of grasshopper.
All other winged insects with four legs are disgusting to you.
These will make you unclean: anyone who touches their dead bodies will be unclean until evening.
Anyone who picks up any part of their dead bodies must wash his clothes, and he will be unclean until evening.
Every animal with a hoof that is not fully split in two, or that does not chew the cud, is unclean for you. Anyone who touches them will be unclean.
Of all the animals that walk on four legs, those that walk on paws are unclean for you. Anyone who touches their dead bodies will be unclean until evening.
Anyone who carries their dead bodies must wash his clothes, and he will be unclean until evening. They are unclean for you.
Of the small animals that move along the ground, these are unclean for you: the weasel, the rat, any kind of large lizard,
the gecko, the monitor lizard, the wall lizard, the skink, and the chameleon.
Of all the creatures that move along the ground, these are unclean for you. Anyone who touches them when they are dead will be unclean until evening.

If one of them dies and falls on something, that thing becomes unclean. Whether it is made of wood, cloth, leather, or sackcloth, whatever it is used for, it must be put in water. It will be unclean until evening, and then it will be clean.
If one of them falls into a clay pot, everything in the pot becomes unclean, and you must break the pot.
Any food that could be eaten, if water from such a pot gets on it, becomes unclean. Any drink in such a pot becomes unclean.
Anything that part of their dead body falls on becomes unclean. If it is an oven or a cooking stove, it must be broken to pieces. They are unclean, and you must treat them as unclean.
But a spring or a well that holds water stays clean. Yet anyone who touches the dead body in it becomes unclean.
If part of a dead body falls on seed that is to be planted, the seed stays clean.
But if water has been put on the seed and part of a dead body falls on it, it is unclean for you.
If an animal that you are allowed to eat dies by itself, anyone who touches its dead body will be unclean until evening.
Anyone who eats some of its dead body must wash his clothes, and he will be unclean until evening. Anyone who carries its dead body must also wash his clothes, and he will be unclean until evening.
Every small creature that moves along the ground is disgusting. Do not eat it.
Do not eat any creature that moves along the ground, whether it crawls on its belly, walks on four legs, or has many legs. They are disgusting.
Do not make yourselves disgusting or unclean by any of these crawling creatures. Do not let them make you unclean.
For I am the LORD your God. Make yourselves holy and be holy, because I am holy. Do not make yourselves unclean with any creature that moves along the ground.
I am the LORD who brought you out of Egypt to be your God. So be holy, because I am holy.
This is the teaching about animals, birds, every living creature that moves in the water, and every creature that moves along the ground.
It helps you to know the difference between what is unclean and what is clean, and between the animals that may be eaten and those that may not be eaten."
